prompt: Explain the federal budget using only football metaphors. Do not stop when they stop working.
response:
Alright, let’s break down the federal budget using nothing but football metaphors. No quitting when the analogies get strained—we’re running this play all the way to the end zone.

### 1. The Playbook = The President’s Budget Proposal
Every season starts with the head coach (the President) drawing up a massive playbook in February. It’s a wish list of trick plays, deep passes, and goal-line stands. It says, “We’re going to throw for 500 yards, run the wishbone, and never punt.” The other team’s coaches (Congress) grab a red pen and laugh, because the head coach doesn’t call the actual plays on Sunday.

### 2. The Offensive Coordinator = Congress (Specifically the House)
In this league, the head coach doesn’t call the plays; the Offensive Coordinator (the House of Representatives) does. They rip pages out of the head coach’s playbook, draw up their own routes, and decide who gets the ball. If the OC wants to run a flea-flicker on 4th and 1 (fund a new border wall) while the head coach wanted a screen pass (climate subsidies), the OC wins. The money is the football—you cannot snap the ball without the OC’s approval.

### 3. The Two-Minute Drill = Continuing Resolutions
When the play clock is running out and the offense can’t agree on a full set of plays, they call a timeout. A Continuing Resolution is the legislative equivalent of spiking the ball to stop the clock. You don’t gain yards; you just keep doing exactly what you did last down, hoping you don’t fumble the season away while you argue in the huddle.

### 4. The Salary Cap = The Debt Ceiling
The league has a hard salary cap (the debt ceiling). The problem is, the front office already signed all the players to massive, guaranteed contracts (mandatory spending). Now the bill comes due, and the team has to vote to raise the cap just to pay the players they already have. If they don’t raise the cap, the league dissolves the franchise (default). It’s a vote to pay the credit card bill for the keg stands you did at the Super Bowl party last year.

### 5. The Depth Chart = Mandatory Spending
This is the roster you cannot cut.
